# CP2 — Per-model MMN waveform comparison, and which two models go on the main slides

**Generated by** `aux/analysis_presentation/per_model_top5.py` (2026-08-17).
**Site** FCz electrode · **read-out** mTRF · **six models**, whisper-large excluded at load.
**Criteria** the committed S7: trough in 100–240 ms, ≥ 0.75 µV deep, ≥ 50 % recovery within 120 ms.
**No deviance restriction** — this is a head-to-head of best responders, not a dose–response.

---

## Recommendation

**Main slide 1 — `whisper-small`. Main slide 2 — `wav2vec2-medium`. Runner-up — `whisper-base`.**

> **Revised 2026-08-17** after the four wav2vec2 mapping JSONs were pulled from the cluster. The
> first version of this memo recommended whisper-small + whisper-base, with wav2vec2-medium as
> runner-up *because its held-out r was unknown and a question about fit quality could not be
> answered on the spot*. That was the only thing holding it back. The number turned out to be
> **+0.223 — the second-highest of the six** — so the objection is gone and wav2vec2-medium beats
> whisper-base on every column except a marginally smaller depth gap. Nothing else moved: no figure,
> no trough, no S7 verdict.

| | why |
|---|---|
| **whisper-small** | The clearest *visual* story. The largest clean literature→Phase-2 gap: median trough −1.32 → −3.05 µV, a **2.3× deepening** with no single outlier carrying it (its Phase-2 rank 5 is still −2.93 µV). All 10 panels pass S7. Its Phase-2 row is the best-shaped row in the whole set — 5/5 control-window specific, 0/5 down-sloping, median post-trough slope **+3.95 µV/100 ms**: every trace returns monotonically to baseline by ~300 ms. |
| **wav2vec2-medium** | The strongest *statistical* story, and the other architecture family. The **highest S7 pass rate of any model on both sets** — 60.4 % of 48 literature and **73.6 % of 254 Phase-2** conditions — which is a strictly like-for-like comparison (same stimuli, same criteria, same electrode). Now also the **second-highest held-out mapping r (+0.223)**, so the model with the most reliable MMN is not a poor fit to the EEG. 9/10 clean panels, 0/5 down-sloping in Phase 2. Its gap is the smallest of the four viable models (−1.05 µV), which is the trade being made. |
| **runner-up: whisper-base** | Same shape as whisper-small and a slightly larger gap than wav2vec2-medium (−1.16 vs −1.05 µV), all 10 panels passing S7. Displaced because wav2vec2-medium beats it on pass rate (.604/.736 vs .271/.480), on fit (+0.223 vs +0.173) and on Phase-2 recovery fraction (1.07 vs 0.72) — and because two adjacent whisper models make a narrower pair of slides than one model from each family. |

**⚠️ Do not quote the r column across architectures.** wav2vec2 was mapped on 10 s/10 s windows
against whisper's 30 s/10 s (both `pca_var=None`), so "wav2vec2 has the best held-out r" is **not**
evidence that wav2vec2 predicts EEG better than whisper — both handoffs call the whisper ballpark a
*loose sanity gate* for wav2vec2, not an exact comparison. Its legitimate use here is exactly what it
is used for: removing a "we don't know whether that model even fits" objection to wav2vec2-medium,
and ranking within a family. The like-for-like argument for wav2vec2-medium is the **S7 pass rate**,
which shares stimuli, criteria and site with every other model in the table.

### Why not the other three

- **wav2vec2-large** — now has the highest held-out r of the six (+0.244) and the biggest median gap
  (−3.87 µV), so it is the model most likely to be reached for. It is still **the one model that
  fails on the exact objection already raised**, and r does not fix shape. Two of its ten panels fail
  S7 (literature 2000→1000 Hz, Phase-2 1745→7611 Hz), both because the trace never recovers —
  recovery fractions 0.29 and 0.19 against a 0.50 requirement. Its literature rank-1 panel
  (1850→1000 Hz) is scored at −7.90 µV but has a **post-trough slope of −1.54 µV/100 ms**: still
  falling at the end of the readout, precisely the down-sloping shape that drew the question last
  time. Only 7 of 10 panels are clean. And its best literature stimulus (−7.90 µV) essentially ties
  its best Phase-2 one (−8.05 µV), so the head-to-head has no headline. Reach for it only if depth is
  being prioritised over shape, and expect the shape question.
- **whisper-medium** — its Phase-2 row is genuinely excellent (median −3.99 µV, recovery 2.50, 5/5
  specific, 0 down-sloping), but its **literature** row is led by a −9.61 µV outlier (`method_43`,
  633→700 Hz) that is deeper than anything in its Phase-2 row. On a head-to-head slide that inverts
  the message: literature wins the "best single stimulus" comparison by +4.94 µV. It also has the
  **lowest held-out r of the six (+0.079)**, and the outlier sets the shared y-axis so the other nine
  panels are visibly flattened.
- **whisper-tiny** — the cleanest panels of all (10/10) and a respectable r (+0.212), but essentially
  **no story**: median gap −0.24 µV and best-trough gap +0.02 µV. Its literature and Phase-2 rows
  look the same, which is a true and interesting result for the appendix and a dead slide for the
  main deck.

so `chosen_layer` survived as a shell constant while `test_r_chosen`, which lives only in the JSON,

**The four files were pulled from `jed` on 2026-08-17 and all six models now report a real r.** The
command, kept for the next time this happens:

```bash
rsync -av "jed:/work/upschrimpf1/sigfstea/multimodal-brain-scaling/outputs/results/eeg_mapping/"'wav2vec2-*__*__D2.json' \
      outputs/results/eeg_mapping/
```

`per_model_top5.py` needed no change to consume them — `heldout_test_r()` reads the JSON when

`blocks.12`, `encoder.layers.2`, `encoder.layers.12`) — which independently confirms the hardcoded

## The evidence table

`model_choice_evidence.csv`, one row per model. Depth first (the visual story), then the criteria
rates, then shape quality, then fit.

| model | LIT top-5 best / median µV | P2 top-5 best / median µV | **gap (median)** | S7 rate LIT (n=48) | S7 rate P2 (n=254) | P2 median recovery | P2 down-sloping | clean panels /10 | held-out r |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| whisper-tiny | −2.65 / −2.17 | −2.63 / −2.41 | −0.24 | 0.333 | 0.492 | 1.31 | 0/5 | **10** | +0.212 |
| whisper-base | −1.34 / −1.24 | −2.65 / −2.39 | −1.16 | 0.271 | 0.480 | 0.72 | 0/5 | 9 | +0.173 |
| **whisper-small** | −1.49 / −1.32 | −3.33 / −3.05 | **−1.73** | 0.312 | 0.496 | 1.59 | 0/5 | 9 | +0.118 |
| whisper-medium | −9.61 / −2.30 | −4.67 / −3.99 | −1.69 | 0.542 | 0.610 | 2.50 | 0/5 | 9 | +0.079 |
| **wav2vec2-medium** | −2.08 / −1.88 | −3.79 / −2.93 | −1.05 | **0.604** | **0.736** | 1.07 | 0/5 | 9 | +0.223 |
| wav2vec2-large | −7.90 / −3.76 | −8.05 / −7.63 | −3.87 | 0.542 | 0.555 | 0.84 | 0/5 | **7** | **+0.244** |

The r column is `test_r_chosen` averaged over the 47 NC-surviving electrodes, at each model's own
committed mapping layer, from `outputs/results/eeg_mapping/<model>__electrodes__D2.json`. **Read it
within an architecture, not across one** — see the note under the recommendation.

**Reading the shape columns.** Three independent quantities, none of them invented for this figure:

1. **`recovery_frac`** — the S2 quantity: the fraction of its own depth the trace climbs back within
   120 ms of the trough. ≥ 0.50 is required to pass. Higher = a cleaner dip-and-recover.
2. **`s4_specificity`** — the committed S4 criterion: is the scored trough more negative than the
   deepest point of the 300–440 ms control window? **False means the trace's real minimum is later**,
   so what got scored at 100–240 ms is the shoulder of a ramp that is still descending.
3. **`post_slope_uv_per_100ms`** — OLS slope of the µV trace from the trough to 360 ms. Positive =
   returns toward baseline over the whole readout; **negative = the "down-sloping effect
   afterwards"** raised about one literature panel. Only three panels in the entire 60 are negative
   (whisper-base LIT-1 at −0.06, effectively flat; whisper-medium LIT-2 at −0.47;
   **wav2vec2-large LIT-1 at −1.54**, the one real offender).

"Clean panels /10" = passes S7 **and** S4 **and** has a positive post-trough slope.

**One caveat on the recommended pair.** whisper-small's literature rank-4 panel (1850→1000 Hz,
`method_19_counter`) passes S7 but **fails S4** — its 300–440 ms window is as negative as the scored
trough. It is one of two blemishes across the 20 recommended panels — the other is
wav2vec2-medium's literature rank-4 panel, described below — and both are in row A, never row B. If
the slide should be question-proof, drop it and promote the next distinct pair,
`method_44` (633→1000 Hz, −0.99 µV, S4 ✓, slope +0.59) — the row's median trough is **unchanged at
−1.32 µV**, so the story does not move. Deliberately
**not** done automatically — silently dropping a panel because of how it looks is the thing this
analysis exists to avoid. wav2vec2-medium's one blemish is the mirror image: its literature rank-4
panel (1850→1000 Hz) also passes S7 but fails S4; its Phase-2 row is 5/5 clean. Neither recommended
model has a down-sloping panel in either row.

## Decisions this analysis had to make

### 1. Ranking rule — each model's own top 5, not the consensus top 5

The existing per-model figures (`literature_waveforms__<model>.png`,
`phase2_waveforms__<model>.png` in `aux/analysis_novel_search/plots/`) show **the same ten stimuli
in every model's figure**: they de-overlay the *consensus* ranking — `rank_directions()` sorts by
`n_agree` (how many of the six models pass S7) then by `mean_uv` over the agreeing models. **Confirmed,
not assumed:** `plot_instance_waveforms_per_model()` takes `ranked.head(n)` from that one shared
ordering and merely splits it by model. A model that dislikes the consensus set is shown its own weak
responses there.

This deliverable ranks **each model by its own `trough_uv` at FCz, most negative first**, separately
within the literature set and within Phase 2. Both views are kept — the consensus figures are
untouched.

### 2. De-duplication of the literature row — **5 distinct ordered frequency pairs**

The 24 literature methods collapse onto far fewer stimuli: **ten** of them are 1000→1200 Hz, **five**
are 1000→1850 Hz and **two** are 1000→1500 Hz — distinct papers that share a frequency pair and
differ only in SOA, tone duration or intensity. Across both directions the 48 instances cover only
**20 distinct ordered pairs**.

Undeduplicated, this is not hypothetical. whisper-tiny's raw literature top 5 is
`method_19_counter, method_18_counter, method_17_counter, method_60_counter, method_55_counter` —
**three of the five slots are the same 1850→1000 Hz pair.** whisper-base's raw top 5 is *all
five* the 1000↔1850 Hz pair.

**Rule applied: five distinct ordered (standard → deviant) frequency pairs, keeping the
deepest-troughing instance of each.** *Ordered*, so 1000→1850 and 1850→1000 remain two different
stimuli — collapsing them would erase the direction asymmetry the counterbalancing exists to measure.
Applied to the literature row only; the Phase-2 grid has no duplicate pairs by construction, so the
rule is a no-op there and is left switched off to keep that visible. The un-deduplicated ranking is
written out in full to `per_model_full_ranking.csv`, so what the rule removed is auditable.

*(The current across-model figure does **not** dedupe — that is why 1000→1850 Hz appears three times
on it.)*

### 3. y-axis — shared within a figure, **never** across models

Each figure shares one y-axis across its ten panels, so row A and row B are directly comparable.
**A shared axis across models is not legible.** The deepest top-5 trough is whisper-medium's
−9.61 µV; the shallowest is whisper-tiny's −2.65 µV, a **3.6× range** — and that understates it,
because the medians span −1.24 µV (whisper-base) to −7.63 µV (wav2vec2-large), a **6.2× range**. One
common axis would compress whisper-base's traces into ~16 % of the axis height. Per-model scaling is
required; each figure says so on its face.

Within whisper-medium the shared axis is itself strained by the −9.61 µV literature outlier, which is
part of why that model is not recommended for the main deck. `--free_y` autoscales every panel for
inspection; the deck figures use the shared axis.

## Figure captions

Each figure is `plots/per_model_top5/<model>.png` with a byte-reproducible SVG twin at
`svgs/per_model_top5/<model>.svg`.

> **Generic caption (all six figures).** FCz difference wave — the mean of 15 deviant realizations
> minus the standard, mean-baseline-corrected over the 3×SOA pre-onset window, in microvolts,
> predicted by the frozen mTRF mapping for this model at its committed electrode layer. **Row A is
> this model's own five best literature conditions and row B its own five best model-selected
> (Phase-2) conditions, where "best" means the most negative trough in the 100–240 ms scoring window
> as scored for *this model alone* — not the six-model consensus ranking used elsewhere in the
> memo.** Row A shows five *distinct* ordered frequency pairs (the deepest instance of each), because
> ten literature methods share the 1000→1200 Hz pair and five share 1000→1850 Hz. The shaded band is
> the scoring window and ▾ marks the scored trough; each panel is annotated with its standard →
> deviant frequencies, its direction, its trough in µV and latency, and this model's own S7 verdict
> (trough ≤ −0.75 µV **and** ≥ 50 % recovery within 120 ms) — a red title is a fail. The y-axis is
> shared across all ten panels of one figure and is **not** comparable between figures: the six
> models' predicted µV scales differ by up to 6×.

Per-model sentences to append:

- **whisper-small** *(main slide 1)* — median trough deepens −1.32 → −3.05 µV; all ten panels pass
  S7; every Phase-2 trace returns monotonically to baseline (median post-trough slope +3.95 µV/100 ms).
  The literature rank-4 panel passes S7 but not the 300–440 ms control-window check.
- **whisper-base** *(runner-up)* — median trough deepens −1.24 → −2.39 µV; all ten panels pass S7;
  the literature row sits barely above the 0.75 µV floor (rank 5 is −0.80 µV), which is itself the
  point of the comparison.
- **wav2vec2-medium** *(main slide 2)* — the highest criterion pass rate of any model (73.6 % of
  its 254 Phase-2 conditions) and the second-highest held-out mapping r (+0.223), with the smallest
  depth gap of the viable models (−1.88 → −2.93 µV): the argument here is reliability, not
  amplitude. Its literature rank-4 panel passes S7 but not the 300–440 ms control-window check.
- **whisper-medium** — the lowest held-out r of the six (+0.079); the strongest Phase-2 row (median −3.99 µV, median recovery 2.50)
  set against a literature row led by a −9.61 µV outlier, `method_43` (633→700 Hz), that is deeper
  than anything in Phase 2 and sets the shared axis.
- **wav2vec2-large** — the highest held-out r of the six (+0.244), the largest median gap
  (−3.87 µV), and the weakest shapes: two of ten panels
  fail S7 for want of recovery, and the literature rank-1 trace is still descending at the end of
  the readout (post-trough slope −1.54 µV/100 ms).
- **whisper-tiny** — the cleanest panels of the six and the smallest gap (−0.24 µV median, +0.02 µV
  on the best stimulus): for this model the model-selected stimuli are not better than the
  literature ones.

## Validation performed (all passed)

| check | result |
|---|---|
| exactly 6 models, whisper-large absent | ✅ asserted at load, filtered in `load_scored` |
| 48 literature and 254 Phase-2 direction-instances | ✅ |
| every regular condition has its counter counterpart; direction carried explicitly | ✅ asserted per set |
| trough sign convention — every top-5 trough negative | ✅ (a positive one raises `SystemExit`) |
| derived `trough_uv` reproduces the committed scored CSVs | ✅ **5.0 × 10⁻⁶ µV** max deviation over 1,812 rows (the CSVs round to 5 dp) |
| top-5 values reproduce `literature_top48.csv` / `phase2_top50.csv` for ≥ 2 models | ✅ **48 values, MATCH** (whisper-tiny, whisper-base; checked against `mean/median/min/max_uv_all6`, the only µV columns those tables carry) |
| every panel is a mean of 15 deviants | ✅ all 1,812 cells; none excluded |
| each sweep's `chosen_layer` equals the layer the predictions were written at | ✅ all 6 (`blocks.0`, `blocks.0`, `blocks.1`, `blocks.12`, `encoder.layers.2`, `encoder.layers.12`) — confirms the hardcoded shell constants against the sweep output |
| continuity with the across-model figure | ✅ 2263→7611 Hz is in whisper-small's Phase-2 top 5; 1600→3200 Hz is in wav2vec2-large's |
| `outputs/results_soafix_full` vs `outputs/results_soafix` at (FCz, mTRF, X=0.75) | ✅ byte-identical slices, so this analysis and `literature_results.py` read the same numbers |

**Modified** — no *committed* script, figure or CSV was touched at any point. Within this task's
own new module, `per_model_top5.py` gained a `chosen_layer` assertion in `heldout_test_r()` on

**Command**
```bash
cd /Users/sophiesigfstead/Documents/multimodal-brain-scaling-2
PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD/scripts" conda run -n mbs-env \
    python aux/analysis_presentation/per_model_top5.py
# inspection variant, every panel autoscaled:
PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD/scripts" conda run -n mbs-env \

```

**Why a new module rather than an edit to `phase1_results.py`.** That module is phase-scoped — one
source per invocation, under a `phase1_`/`phase2_` prefix — and its figures are cited by path from
`novel_stimulus_search_results.md`. This figure needs *both* sources in one render and a different
ranking key, so it lives beside the other presentation deliverable (`trough_distributions.py`) and
**imports** rather than restates everything that must not drift: the trace construction
(`load_fcz_waves`), the layer map, the x-window, the scoring window, the palette, the direction
convention (`load_literature`, `_with_std_dev`), the ranking loader (`load_scored`,
`rank_directions`), the shape statistics (`trace_stats`, `decide`) and the exact criteria knobs
(`WINDOW`, `RECOVERY_MS`, `RECOVERY_FRAC`, `CTRL_WINDOW`, `EDGE_GUARD_BINS`). Nothing is re-scored.
